findings.title: round.schema.json's scripts_refreshed shape was tightened with no MAJOR bump, invalidating an already-frozen closed round
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl :: refresh_scripts / record_build! (the new record shape the schema now demands)

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md D7 and the diff's own removed round.schema.json docstring (both naming round 2026-09-12-check-docs-01 as a round whose scripts_refreshed entry was written under the old two-field shape)
Project.toml (unchanged at both ends of the diff)
findings.before: schema/round.schema.json required only `["at", "head"]` on every scripts_refreshed entry, matching what `refresh_scripts` (base) wrote: `entry = Dict{String,Any}("at" => timestamp(), "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40))`. The base docstring of this very schema field states: '...2026-09-12-check-docs-01 hit exactly that, and the copies were refreshed by hand. A refresh is legitimate and must stay VISIBLE, so every one is appended here...' — i.e. that closed, frozen round's ROUND.toml already carries a scripts_refreshed entry in this two-field shape.
findings.after: The same field now requires `["at", "head", "reason", "after_pass", "scripts"]`, three of them brand new, `additionalProperties: false` on the sub-object. `config_sha`'s pattern was also widened in the same file. `git show 3e30907:Project.toml` and `git show 54cd7f2:Project.toml` both report `version = "1.0.0"` — no MAJOR bump accompanies either schema edit, and the round record's own `schema_version` field ("the tool MAJOR this artefact was written under", per this same schema file) therefore records the SAME value (1) for a round written under the old shape and one written under the new — nothing distinguishes them at read time. `RoundFiles.read_round` validates every ROUND.toml against the CURRENT schema unconditionally (no schema_version branch), so the pre-existing 2026-09-12-check-docs-01 record now fails validation, is reported by `RoundFiles.rounds()` as `state = :invalid`, and trips the doctor's `ROUND.MARKER` check to FAIL — a check `gbg doctor --deep` runs, which `gbg release` requires green.
findings.why_it_matters: §5.5 states plainly that changing any schema is MAJOR — this is the tool's own closed-vocabulary discipline, restated in ARCHITECTURE §6.3 ('Every artefact carries schema_version... Changing any vocabulary is MAJOR'), precisely so that a shape change can be told apart from what came before. Skipping the bump here does not just break the abstract rule: it retroactively invalidates a specific, already-closed, already-frozen round this same commit set (and the base ARCHITECTURE text) names by id, with no migration or exemption offered for it. The developers evidently anticipated a schema-refused record in general (the new `load()` catches it as exit 2, and a new test in test/rounds.jl exercises exactly this path against an artificially-corrupted record) but nothing back-fills or grandfathers the real historical record this diff itself documents as already existing in the old shape, and 'a round is tracked, frozen' (D10) forecloses hand-editing it to add the new fields after the fact. Left as is, the tool's own self-application (Consumer #5) would fail `ROUND.MARKER` and, by extension, its own release gate, until someone works around the very freeze the architecture is built to guarantee.
findings.description: The scripts_refreshed sub-schema and config_sha pattern in schema/round.schema.json were both edited to match the new refresh_scripts/record_build! machinery this diff adds, but the edit widens (config_sha) and tightens (scripts_refreshed, via three new required fields) the same artefact's schema without the MAJOR bump §5.5 requires for any schema change, and without reconciling the tightening against the pre-existing closed round the diff's own prose says already holds an entry in the old, now-noncompliant shape.
